This is a microscopy image showing multi-septate fungal spores with a beak-like projection, light olive-brown color, approximately 20-50 µm. This strongly suggests Alternaria conidia. The symptom description mentions "hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell."

Let me view one reference image from each of 4 candidate classes before finalizing.

The test image is a microscopy image (scale bar 20 µm) of fungal conidia with:
- Muriform (multi-septate, transverse + longitudinal septa) structure
- Ovoid to oblong/clavate shape
- Tapering beak at the apical end on several spores
- Light olive-brown to golden-brown color
- ~20-50 µm in size

This perfectly matches the Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers KB description: *"light olive brown to dark brown, hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell on the terminal end, and are 7-18 x 18-50 µm in size."*

The reference images for the other 3 classes (Early_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Anthracnose) all show macroscopic field symptoms, none matching this microscopic spore morphology. Anthracnose conidia are unicellular and hyaline (not muriform/brown like these). Septoria produces pycnidiospores that are filiform (needle-like). Early blight is also Alternaria but the spore morphology here specifically matches the described Alternaria stem canker species.
